# QS-CFW-8404-30 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-8404-30 (4140)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-8404-30

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and disposition procedures for flange blank CFW-8404-30 produced from material grade 4140 at Plant P3. The document applies to incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and finished blank releases intended for machining and assembly. It is intended for use by operations, quality, and production engineering personnel responsible for manufacturing and inspection.

## Background and rationale
CFW-8404-30 is a critical forging blank that will be machined to final geometry in subsequent operations. Controlling hardness, bore tolerance, and forging weight is necessary to ensure machinability, dimensional conformity, and material integrity. The specified hardness range provides a balance between strength and machinability for 4140 material in this supplied condition. The bore diameter tolerance ensures adequate fit and concentricity at machining setup. Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure die life, handling capability, and process consistency.

## Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material | 4140 | Per purchase order and material certificate |
| Hardness (as-supplied) | The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. | Hardness measured on heat-affected cross section representative of production lot |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm. | Tolerance applies to nominal bore dimension on drawing prior to finish machining |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 15.0 kg. | Weight measured after trimming and flash removal |

## Inspection method
Inspection shall be performed by certified quality personnel using calibrated equipment and documented practices.

Hardness
- Sampling: Select representative pieces from each production lot. For small lots, select a representative sample consistent with shop standard sampling practice to demonstrate lot conformity.
- Location: Perform hardness readings on the face and rim area representative of the bulk material, avoiding scant flash and heavily worked zones. Multiple indentations may be taken to establish a representative mean and range.
- Equipment: Use Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to appropriate scale and verified with certified reference blocks prior to use.
- Acceptance: Verify that readings fall within The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. If any measured location falls outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter tolerance
- Measurement: Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer capable of reading to the required tolerance. Measurements shall be taken at multiple axial positions and at two orthogonal diameters to detect out-of-round.
- Datum and orientation: Measure relative to drawing datums; ensure part is free of burrs and debris that could affect measurement.
- Acceptance: Verify that measured bore diameter conforms to nominal plus or minus The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm. Document all measurements.

Weight
- Procedure: Determine forging weight after trimming and flash removal using calibrated scales placed on a stable surface. Remove loose debris and any packaging prior to weighing.
- Acceptance: Confirm weight does not exceed The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 15.0 kg. Parts exceeding this value must be segregated and dispositioned.

Surface condition and visual inspection
- Conduct a visual inspection for defects such as laps, folds, cracks, piping, excessive oxide, and unacceptable scale. Document defects and severity to support disposition decisions.

Calibration and equipment
- Use only calibrated measuring and hardness testing equipment. Calibration records shall be current and available in the quality record package.

## Nonconformance handling
When inspection identifies nonconforming conditions, follow the process below to ensure consistent and traceable disposition.

Identification and segregation
- Immediately tag and physically segregate nonconforming parts from conforming inventory. Use clear labeling to prevent inadvertent use.

Containment and notification
- Notify production supervision and quality engineering of nonconforming findings. Provide documented measurement data and relevant heat or lot information from material certificates.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the nonconformance is dimensional and can be corrected by machining without violating design intent or downstream processes, prepare a rework plan. Rework must be reviewed and approved by quality engineering prior to execution.
- Use-as-is with concession: For certain deviations that do not affect function, quality engineering may approve a concession. Concessions require documented justification, affected quantity, and authorization signature.
- Scrapping: Parts that cannot be safely reworked or used shall be scrapped in accordance with scrap control procedures and documented.

Root cause and corrective action
- For recurring nonconformances, initiate a containment and corrective action investigation. Include process review, tooling condition, material certificate verification, and supplier communication where applicable. Implement corrective actions and verify effectiveness before resuming normal production.

Examples
- Example: A sample piece measures a hardness slightly below the lower bound specified by The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. Quality will segregate the lot, review heat treatment records, and either reheat or request supplier corrective action depending on root cause analysis.
- Example: A bore measurement reads beyond The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm at multiple positions. The lot is segregated and reviewed for die wear; parts may be reworked if material remains within machining allowance and quality approves.

## Records to keep
Maintain QA records for each lot and retained documentation in the document control system. Required records include:
- Incoming material certificate and traceability to forging heat
- Hardness test reports and calibration verification for hardness equipment
- Bore diameter measurement logs with gauge identification and calibration status
- Weighing records showing measured weight and scale calibration
- Nonconformance reports, disposition documents, and corrective action records
- Final release authorization

Retention of records shall follow plant archival practice and be available for audit.
